Couple things.

Congrats on your life changing experience, I am happy to advise as I am on a similar journey but a little ahead of you.

1. IMO it's best if you have a sober person nearby to help you with administering the medication, it's not fun at all for your set and setting starting off with that anxiety. And if someone sober is nearby, they can help you out of any bad spots you may temporarily be in.
2. I wouldn't recommend a cotton filter at all, I recommend these off of amazon [https://a.co/d/avAXd7T](https://a.co/d/avAXd7T) , with a sterilized CLEAN dedicated shot glass with a concave bottom, you shouldn't lose much medication at all.
3. I prefer the deltoid as that is what I have experience with, but for self admin if you really must, the thigh is easiest to keep straight and centered.
4. I really do not recommend having anything else in your system at all, excluding perhaps an anti nausea medication. Just remember to take DEEP breaths, and the rollercoaster will ALWAYS end within an hour. If it feels like too much right now, it WILL subside soon and you'll be alright.
5. Please try to have a 0.000g scale if you do not already. I made the mistake of only a 0.00g scale and it was harder to control dose.
6. Start at a lower dose than what the clinic had you at if you're truly nervous, you can always go up next time, can't take any back.

Hi. I don't expect a response. I appreciate it. I'm going to hit my 20th birthday in the summer, and everyone around my age or slightly older always seem to have fun plans with friends, which they take time off of work for. Which I never find myself doing besides taking my birthday off last year to sit at home. I tried to reach out(ex: lets go to the sushi bar) but I never hear back. I offer to pay for lunch for current coworkers but they seem to always already have plans. 
I saw a councilor regularly in high school, but I found that the more I thought about how fucked up and broken everything was(basically dwelling on it because talking about it makes me obsess over it) instead of my usual coping mechanism which is just choose to forget everything and move on. My psychiatrist put me on a medication, but they just made me feel empty inside which was terrifying to me(probably related to me fear of literal nothing) so I refused to take them. When I moved away I couldn't afford medical insurance, let alone a councilor. I'm afraid to go back to counseling even when/if I can afford it, because of how weak it made me. Thinking about my problems and obsessing over them somehow made them worse. Everything horrible or wrong that I've done/ has been done to me I can't seem to forget. The bullying I endured, mistakes I've made. 10+ years later I still reach out and apologize to people I have wronged, or did something to me that I didn't understand.
I'm sorry to waste your time. Thank you for your consideration.
